proposal: The Mandate recommends that the Secret Service hand all investigations unrelated to protection to the Departments of Justice and Treasury, begin closing field offices not taken over by those departments, and move field agents into ICE offices, keeping only HSI-directed work tracing finances tied to illegal immigration. It also recommends that the Secret Service keep visitor logs for all facilities where the President works or resides, significantly increase Uniformed Division staffing, and let Uniformed Division officers enforce all applicable laws beyond the White House vicinity.

status_summary: No transfer of Secret Service financial or cyber investigations to Justice or Treasury, and no field office closure plan, was found. CRS analysis of the FY2027 DHS budget request (dated 2026-06-09) describes a Secret Service request of 3.45 billion dollars that adds 520 special agent, 256 Uniformed Division and 50 technical law enforcement positions: the Uniformed Division increase is a proposal that aligns with the Mandate's staffing item, while the agent growth points to the existing dual-mission structure continuing. On visitor logs, a February 2025 news report quoted a White House official as saying visitor logs would not be released in the second term; the Mandate's ask concerns the Secret Service keeping logs, which the sources do not address.

timeline.event: A CRS analysis of the FY2027 DHS budget request (R48979) describes a Secret Service request of 3.45 billion dollars that adds 520 special agent, 256 Uniformed Division and 50 technical law enforcement positions; it describes no transfer of financial or cyber investigations to Justice or Treasury and no field office closure plan.

title: Focus the Secret Service on protection, keep visitor logs, expand the Uniformed Division
uncertainties: Absence of evidence from a limited search: a Secret Service reorganization could exist without surfacing in the sources read. The CRS report was read only in part. The Uniformed Division position increase is in the FY2027 request; whether FY2026 appropriations funded similar increases was not checked. The visitor log report concerns publication of White House logs by the administration, not whether the Secret Service keeps them, so it is context only and not a timeline event. The structural split of the Secret Service between DOJ and Treasury in the DHS dismantling plan (page 134) is tracked in c05-01; this record covers the component-level recommendations on pages 157 and 158. Bills in the current Congress on moving Secret Service functions were not located. The FY2027 request's release date was not pinned, so it is described from the CRS analysis and not entered as a timeline event.
